def-fd-solenoidal-surrogate-residual:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $T>0$, and $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized volume $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For a vector field $w$, use the componentwise Fourier coefficients $\widehat w(k)=\int_{Q_d}w(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$ and norm $\|w\|_2=(\int_{Q_d}|w(x)|^2\,d\mu(x))^{1/2}$. Define $P_0=I$ and, for $k\ne0$, $P_k=I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2$, with $\widehat{Pw}(k)=P_k\widehat w(k)$; $P$ is the Leray projector. For a vector field $w$, $\operatorname{div}w=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jw_j$; for a tensor field $F=(F_{ij})$, set $(\operatorname{div}F)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_{ij}$, and set $(v\otimes v)_{ij}=v_i v_j$. Let $\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j^2$. A field is called solenoidal when it is divergence-free. Given a constant $\nu\ge0$, smooth $f:[0,T]\times Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, a smooth solenoidal field $v:[0,T]\times Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, and a smooth solenoidal reference initial field $u_0:Q_d\to\mathbb R^d$, define the continuous residual and initial defect by

$$r_v:=\partial_t v+P\operatorname{div}(v\otimes v)-\nu\Delta v-Pf,\qquad d_0:=\|v(0,\cdot)-u_0\|_2.$$

The residual is a continuous function of time with values in $L^2(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$, so $\int_0^T\|r_v(t,\cdot)\|_2\,dt$ is finite. This is a continuous-domain residual: finitely many collocation values do not by themselves bound this $L^1_tL^2_x$ quantity. All quantities here are mathematical; no physical units are assigned to $\nu$.
thm-fd-surrogate-residual-error:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $T>0$, and $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. Use $\|w\|_2=(\int_{Q_d}|w|^2d\mu)^{1/2}$ and let $P$ act on vector Fourier coefficients by $\widehat{Pw}(0)=\widehat w(0)$ and $\widehat{Pw}(k)=(I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2)\widehat w(k)$ for $k\ne0$. Define $\operatorname{div}w=\sum_j\partial_jw_j$, $(\operatorname{div}F)_i=\sum_j\partial_jF_{ij}$, $(w\otimes z)_{ij}=w_i z_j$, and $\Delta=\sum_j\partial_j^2$. Let $\nu\ge0$, $f\in C^\infty([0,T]\times Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$, $u_0\in C^\infty(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$, and $u,v\in C^\infty([0,T]\times Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$ all be divergence-free. Suppose $u(0)=u_0$ and

$$\partial_tu+P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)-\nu\Delta u=Pf,$$

and define $r_v=\partial_tv+P\operatorname{div}(v\otimes v)-\nu\Delta v-Pf$. Put $A(t)=\int_0^t\sup_{x\in Q_d}\|\nabla u(s,x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,ds$, where $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is the Euclidean matrix operator norm. Then for every $t\in[0,T]$,

$$\|v(t)-u(t)\|_2\le e^{A(t)}\left(\|v(0)-u_0\|_2+\int_0^t e^{-A(s)}\|r_v(s)\|_2\,ds\right).$$

This is a conditional estimate for an already given smooth exact solution; it proves no existence theorem and gives no error guarantee from finitely many collocation residual values alone. All quantities are mathematical, with no physical units assigned to $\nu$.
prop-fd-surrogate-law-shift-observable:
## Statement

Let $(\mathcal Z,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space and let $\mu$ be a probability measure on it, meaning a countably additive measure on $\Sigma$ with $\mu(\mathcal Z)=1$. Let $X$ be a real normed vector space and give it the norm-Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by its norm-open sets. Let $S,\widetilde S:\mathcal Z\to X$ be measurable maps. Let $J:X\to\mathbb R$ be $L$-Lipschitz, meaning $|J(x)-J(y)|\le L\|x-y\|_X$ for all $x,y\in X$, with $L\ge0$. Suppose

$$\int_{\mathcal Z}\bigl(\|S\|_X^2+\|\widetilde S\|_X^2\bigr)\,d\mu<\infty,\qquad \int_{\mathcal Z}\|S-\widetilde S\|_X^2\,d\mu\le\varepsilon^2$$

for some finite $\varepsilon\ge0$. For a measurable scalar function $h$, write $\|h\|_{L^2(\mu)}=(\int_{\mathcal Z}|h|^2\,d\mu)^{1/2}$. Let $g:\mathcal Z\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable with $\int g\,d\mu=1$ and $g\le C$ $\mu$-almost everywhere for a finite $C\ge1$, and define the target probability law by $\nu(E)=\int_Eg\,d\mu$ for $E\in\Sigma$, with target expectation $\mathbb E_\nu[H]=\int Hg\,d\mu$ whenever the integral exists. Then the measurable scalar observables $J\circ S$ and $J\circ\widetilde S$ are $\nu$-integrable and

$$\left|\mathbb E_\nu[J(S)]-\mathbb E_\nu[J(\widetilde S)]\right|\le L\sqrt C\,\varepsilon.$$

The estimate assumes a population mean-square error under $\mu$ and a bounded target density $g$; a finite test sample by itself establishes neither assumption. The state space may represent fluid fields when that measurable state model is supplied. For a physical application, both observables must use the same declared scalar unit; this mathematical proposition assigns no physical units.
